<target>### **2.3.1. Reserved Writes Preserve Values, Reads Ignore Values (WPRI)**

Some whole read/write fields are reserved for future use. Software should ignore the values read from these fields, and should preserve the values held in these fields when writing values to other fields of the same register. For forward compatibility, implementations that do not furnish these fields must make them read-only zero. These fields are labeled **WPRI** in the register descriptions.

_To simplify the software model, any backward-compatible future definition of previously reserved fields within a CSR must cope with the possibility that a non-_  _atomic read/modify/write sequence is used to update other fields in the CSR.Alternatively, the original CSR definition must specify that subfields can only be updated atomically, which may require a two-instruction clear bit/set bit sequence in general that can be problematic if intermediate values are not legal._</target>
